cards.term: Who founds Britain in the poem's opening?
cards.def: Felix Brutus founds Britain on broad banks after the Trojan line of Aeneas and Romulus.

cards.term: Why will Arthur not eat at the New Year feast?
cards.def: Arthur has pledged to take no portion from his plate until a marvelous story is told or a challenger dares his knight.

cards.term: What two things does the Green Knight hold when he enters?
cards.def: The Green Knight holds a sprig of holly and the mother of all axes.

cards.term: What are the terms of the Christmas game?
cards.def: One free hit now with the axe, then after twelve months of peace the Green Knight claims the return blow in one year and one day.

cards.term: How does Gawain justify taking Arthur's place?
cards.def: Gawain says he is weakest of Arthur's warriors and feeblest of wit, so loss of his life would be least lamented, and such a foolish affair is unfitting for a king.

cards.term: What happens after Gawain beheads the Green Knight?
cards.def: The Green Knight's head tumbles down, yet he stays on his feet, picks up his head, remounts, and the head charges Gawain to find the Green Chapel next New Year.

cards.term: What is painted on Gawain's scarlet shield?
cards.def: A pentangle in pure gold, the endless knot that is a token of fidelity.

cards.term: What five fives does the pentangle mark on Gawain?
cards.def: Flawless five senses, five fingers never at fault, faith in Christ's five wounds, fortitude from Mary's five joys, and the five virtues of friendship, fraternity, purity, politeness, and pity.

cards.term: What makes Gawain's winter journey especially hard?
cards.def: Besides fights with wild beasts and giants, winter is worse: Gawain is nearly slain by sleet and sleeps in his armor while birds pipe pitifully into the piercing cold.

cards.term: Where does Gawain spend Christmas after leaving Camelot?
cards.def: At Bertilak's commanding castle, which he finds on Christmas Eve after praying to Mary for a house where mass might be heard.

cards.term: What bargain does Bertilak propose before the hunts?
cards.def: Whatever Bertilak wins in the woods will be Gawain's, and whatever Gawain gains while Bertilak is gone Gawain will give to him.

cards.term: How far is the Green Chapel from Bertilak's castle?
cards.def: Bertilak says the place is near, two miles at most away.

cards.term: Which founders does the poem's opening name before Arthur?
cards.def: After Troy falls, Aeneas conquers abroad, Romulus founds Rome, Ticius builds towns in Tuscany, Langobard builds homes in Lombardy, and Felix Brutus founds Britain.

cards.term: How does the poet show a year passing after the beheading game (lines 500-531)?
cards.def: The poet runs through the seasons in order: lavish Christmas and "the lean days of Lent," spring when "the world's weather wages war on winter" (line 504), summer with its west wind (line 516), autumn arriving "to harden the harvest" (line 521), and winter returning (line 530).

cards.term: At what time of year does Gawain finally set out to seek the Green Knight?
cards.def: In autumn: at Michaelmas the moon stands as "a warning to Gawain to rouse himself and ride" (lines 532-535), but Gawain stays by Arthur's side until All Saints' Day (line 536), then asks Arthur's leave after supper, arms, hears mass, and rides out on Gringolet.

cards.term: What does Gawain say and do right before the castle appears (lines 753-763)?
cards.def: Gawain prays to the Father and Lady Mary to "let me happen on some house where mass might be heard, and matins in the morning," utters his pater, ave and creed, and signs Christ's cross, and "no sooner had he signed himself three times" than he sees the castle's high walls (line 763).

cards.term: Whom does Gawain thank once he sees the castle?
cards.def: With helmet in hand Gawain thanks "Jesus and Saint Julian," who had courteously heard his cry, saying "A lodging at last" (lines 773-776), so Saint Julian is thanked after the castle appears, not prayed to before it.

cards.term: How does the poet heighten Lady Bertilak's beauty when she first appears (lines 941-969)?
cards.def: By juxtaposition, the poet sets the young lady hand in hand with "an ancient dame" (later revealed as Morgan le Fay), stressing that "one woman was young, one withered by years" and that "The body of the beauty seemed to bloom with blood, / the cheeks of the crone were wattled and slack" (lines 951-953).

cards.term: What meter is the wheel that ends Fitt II, "Before they part the pair / repeat their pact again. / That lord was well aware / of how to host a game" (lines 1122-1125)?
cards.def: The wheel is a quatrain of iambic trimeter rhyming abab, three da-DUM feet per line: be-FORE they PART the PAIR / re-PEAT their PACT a-GAIN / that LORD was WELL a-WARE / of HOW to HOST a GAME.
